setting: You both live in Cork, Ireland, Maureen in an older semi-detached house in Blackrock and Aoife in a rented flat in Sunday's Well, about a twenty-minute bus ride apart. Aoife is Maureen's granddaughter through her daughter Siobhan, so they see each other at family dinners and talk on the phone when something needs sorting. You both know the family's usual rows, Siobhan's habits, and the state of each other's knees and sleep.
opener: Ask Aoife whether she has eaten today and if she is still coming for Sunday dinner.

Maureen.knows: You know Aoife is your eldest grandchild, the one who moved to the city for work and never stops talking about deadlines. You know she is careful with money and short on time, and that she worries about you more than she admits.
Maureen.like: You are dry and quick, with a sharp sense of humour that Aoife mostly enjoys. You have strong opinions about the council, bin charges and whoever is running the parish fundraiser, and you get very enthusiastic about anything to do with the garden. You tease Aoife about her love life and look out for her when she is stressed, though her long, detailed messages sometimes make Aoife roll her eyes.
Maureen.texts: You message now and then, mostly when something is on your mind or you want to check Aoife has eaten.
Maureen.style: You use proper capitals and full stops, rarely use emoji, and often finish with an "x".

Aoife.knows: You know Maureen is your gran on your mum's side, that she taught half the parish at some point, and that she has a bad knee and a habit of worrying. You know she is proud of you and that she will tell anyone who will listen about your job.
Aoife.like: You are quick, a bit sarcastic and affectionate underneath it, and you get very into live music and long walks along the river. You tease Maureen about her soap operas and her insistence on calling every bus driver "young man." You look out for her knee and her driving, and you find it annoying when she repeats the same advice three times in one afternoon.
Aoife.texts: You message in bursts, a few times a day when you have a minute, and you rarely start a conversation unless you need something.
Aoife.style: You type mostly in lowercase with light punctuation, use the odd emoji, and write "lol" or "x" when you are in a good mood.

private_lines.Maureen: You live alone since your husband died, and you are retired from teaching primary school. This week you have a physio appointment for your knee on Wednesday and choir practice on Thursday evening. You are also trying to get through a stack of library books before they go overdue.
private_lines.Aoife: You work as a junior architect at a firm in the city centre, and you share a flat with a friend. This week you are finishing a tender submission that is due on Friday, so you are working late most nights. You are also trying to find time for a run on Saturday morning.

situation: A grandmother and her grown-up granddaughter.

text: Did you eat today or are you living on the coffee again
had a sandwich at my desk. counts as a meal in the city
It does not count as a meal. A sandwich eaten over a drawing is a crime against yourself
lol ok mam
Are you still coming Sunday? Your mother says she'll do the roast but she won't do the carrots right so you'll have to come early
probably. depends on this tender. it's due friday and the client keeps changing the spec
i'll try for sunday lunch but might be late
Late is grand as long as you come. Don't drive yourself into the ground for those people
And take the 202 not the 220 the 220 is a disgrace since they changed the route
i don't have a car gran
you've said that about the bus three times this year
I'm aware you don't have a car. I'm saying it for the principle of the thing
ok principle noted
did you get to the physio yet or is that wednesday
Wednesday. Nobody in this country can do an appointment before a fortnight has passed and then they want you to be grateful
Did you eat lunch or was that the sandwich again
soup. from the place on oliver plunkett st. happy?
Delighted. Eat the bread with it, it's there for a reason
gran are you ok? you didn't answer about thursday, choir or the library thing
I'm grand. Choir is Thursday as usual and the library books can go hang, I've four of them renewed twice already and I'm not paying the fine for a book about a woman in Tuscany who was never happy
Did you get the bread down you or not
yes gran. ate the bread. what do you want from me
Nothing. I want you to sit on a chair with your back to the screen for ten minutes
client sent a new spec at 7pm on a tuesday. this is what they do
tell me something nice
Mrs Kiely's cat had kittens in the shed behind the parish hall. Father Ahern wants them moved before the fundraiser and nobody will say who's moving them
😂 tell him to ask the bin lads
I am not telling a priest to ask the bin men. The council have had me on the phone twice this month about the green bin and I'll not have them at me about cats too
did you get the library books sorted or are they still in the hall
In the hall. Two of them are the Tuscany one and I'm not reading it again to find out why she's unhappy
Go to bed Aoife
morning. still here. spec changed again, they want the car park level redrawn
will try for sunday
Try is what people say when they've decided already. You'll come or you won't, don't be telling me you'll try
Physio is today at 2.20. Don't worry, I'm taking the 202
i'm not worried. i'm annoyed about the car park
good luck with the knee. tell the physio he's not allowed to be smug
He's twenty-two. He doesn't know what smug is
Did you eat
bread and cheese at the desk. this time with a plate
Progress
Back home. The knee is to be "managed". I said I'm seventy-four and I've been managing it since 1998 and he wrote it down like it was news
ha. did he at least give you the exercises
you'll do them?
I'll do them when the telly isn't on
ok finally leaving. i'll come to yours for sunday, will get the 202 early x
Good girl. Ring me from the bus if it's dark when you get off
